Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones. | trophy id = TrophyTheElder | id = gd_king | type = Boss | summon = [[Ancient Seed]] x3 | behavior = Aggressive | tameable = No | location = * [[Black Forest]] | drops = * [[The Elder Trophy]] * [[Swamp Key]] * [[The Elder Power]] | health 0star = 2500 | damage 0star = * Shoot: 35 Pierce, 20 Chop, 20 Pickaxe * Stomp: 60 Blunt, 1000 Chop, 1000 Pickaxe | abilities = * Root Spawn (25 seconds) * Shoot (6 seconds) * Stomp (5 seconds) | veryweak = Fire | weak = | resistant = | veryresistant = | immune = Poison, Spirit, Stagger | neutral = | aggressive = |faction=Boss}} '''The Elder''' is the second [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a towering humanoid tree-like entity with multiple thin branches sprouting out of his slender, bark-covered body. == Summoning == [[File:TheElderAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|The Elder's Forsaken Altar.]] The Elder's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. His location can be revealed when visiting [[Burial Chambers]] and sometimes ruined structures around Black Forests, where a [[Runestone|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map. He is summoned by placing three {{Item Link|Ancient Seed}}s in his Forsaken altar in Black Forests. Like all bosses, the Elder can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating the Elder|Boss strategies#The Elder}} The Elder has an environment aura that removes darkness and raining. === Root Spawn === The Elder will raise an arm in the air to summon 15 hostile [[Root (creature)|Roots]] within a 15-meter radius circle around the player. Roots can attack players in melee range but are otherwise immobile and will despawn after 18–20 seconds or when The Elder is defeated. Although not typically possible in regular gameplay, a maximum of 30 Roots can be active at once. This ability has a 25-second cooldown and can be used while within 30 meters of a player. === Shoot === A ranged volley of 25 vines directed at a target player (35 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage per hit). This attack has a 6-second cooldown and can be used when a player is 15–50 meters away. He attempts to track players while aiming. Each vine has an initial velocity of 30 meters per second and a spread of 10–20 degrees. They can travel for up to 6 seconds before disappearing. === Stomp === A close-range stomp over a large area (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). It hits in a circle 5 meters in radius from the impact point. This attack can be used when within 3 meters of a player and is accessible every 5 seconds. == Aftermath == Defeating the Elder allows the player to unlock and enter swamp crypts (which are the primary source of [[Scrap Iron]] in the game) with the [[Swamp Key]]. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=The Elder trophy|0star=1}} {{drop row|item=Swamp key|0star=1 per player}} |stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting The Elder’s trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds: * Health regen: +30% * Chop damage: +60% * Pickaxe damage: +60% === Events === Defeating The Elder affects the following [[events]] for that world: * Disables: "The forest is moving..." * Enables: "A foul smell from the swamp..." (if [[Bonemass]] has not been defeated) * Enables: "The ground is shaking." (if a [[Troll]] has died in the world) === Creature spawning === Defeating The Elder unlocks several creatures to spawn at '''night''' in unusual biomes. They can only have 0 stars: * [[Greydwarf Brute]] in Meadows. * [[Greydwarf Shaman]] in Meadows. * [[Draugr]] while it is "Misty" in Meadows, Black Forest, Mountain, Plains. * [[Odin]] in Meadows, Black Forest, Plains. === Traders === Defeating The Elder unlocks the [[Thunder Stone]] and [[Ymir Flesh]] for sale from [[Haldor]]. It also unlocks the [[Woodland Herb Blend]] from [[The Bog Witch]] for 120 [[Coins]]. == Gallery == File:Elder and friends.jpg File:TheElderAltar.png == Notes == * The altar provides a few hints on what items are used to summon him. First, the altar reads "Burn their young" referring to [[Ancient Seed]]s. In addition, the top of the columns are topped by statues that look similar to Ancient Seeds in shape. * Because of The Elder's location in the [[Black Forest]], additional enemies such as [[Troll]]s or [[Greydwarf]]s may join the battle and increase the difficulty significantly, especially at night. * The Elder's high-damage ranged attack can be effective in quickly gathering resources such as [[Wood]], [[Corewood]], [[Stone]], and [[Copper Ore]], without the use of tools. * In the in-game trophies menu, there is another description of The Elder, "Even in death, it seems to grin with secret knowledge." * When The Elder's trophy is mounted on an item mount, he will sometimes say: "Little thing of blood and bone, I should have snapped you like a twig! Now I wither and die, let the great tree have me..." The many names of The Elder: * In the game files, The Elder is also known as "gd_king" as well as "theelder". Likely to be interpreted as "Greydwarf King". * Warnings inscribed in a few of the [[Runestone|runestones]] found in the [[Black Forest]] refer to The Elder as "the One Who Walks" once, and "the Old One" twice:
''Beneath the ground, the roots of the forest twine together on a great loom. Pluck one thread and the whole weave will move. Chop down one tree and all the wood will know. Make yourself known to the One Who Walks, and he will seek you out.''
''Beware the Old One. The ravens say that in ages past he was a shoot of great Yggdrasil itself and a force of wisdom in the days when men and trees were friends. Now he scorns the axe and sets himself against the works of the Gods themselves. Odin banished him here for his pride but his roots are deep.''
''Seven were the creatures banished to this world by mighty Odin in the first days of his kingship. Seven gods and monsters too proud to bear his yoke. I have heard the tread of the Old Ones in the forest and have crouched in the shadow of the Mountain Mother when she flies. Of the others I know little. I will add to this stone when I have seen more.''

To the left of his [[Sacrificial Stones|Sacrificial Stone]] is a small glowing [[Runestone]] called a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]]; interacting with it will add his closest summoning location on the map. He is summoned by placing two {{Item Link|Deer Trophy}} in his Forsaken altar in the Meadows. Like all bosses, Eikthyr can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Eikthyr|Boss strategies#Eikthyr}} Eikthyr has three types of attacks in addition to an environmental aura that forces darkness and removes raining. === Antler === A swiping melee attack with his antlers (20 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack features a 5-second cooldown and can be used when a player is within 4 meters. It has a range of 4.5 meters and hits in a horizontal arc spanning 25 degrees. === Charge === A ranged beam attack that fans out horizontally 45 degrees and extends 20 meters out (15 [[Damage types#Lightning|Lightning]] damage). On contact, the beam will inflict the [[Lightning (effect)|Lightning]] status. This has a 25-second cooldown and Eikthyr can attempt to use this ability when a player is within 15 meters. === Stomp === A 10-meter radius area-of-effect attack that expands outward from the center and inflicts the [[Lightning (effect)|Lightning]] status (15 [[Damage types#Lightning|Lightning]] damage). This attack has a 40-second cooldown. He can use this ability when a player is within 6 meters. == Aftermath == Defeating Eikthyr allows the player to craft the first pickaxe to begin mining ore to create metal tools, weapons, and armor. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Eikthyr trophy|0star=1}} {{drop row|item=Hard antler|0star=3}}|stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting Eikthyr’s trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds: * Run stamina usage: -60% * Jump stamina usage: -60% * Swim stamina usage: -60% === Events === Defeating Eikthyr affects the following [[events]] for that world: * Disables: "Eikthyr rallies the creatures of the forest." * Enables: "The forest is moving..." (if [[The Elder]] hasn't been defeated) === Creature spawning === Defeating Eikthyr unlocks [[Greydwarf]]s to spawn in the Meadows at night. They can only have 0 stars. == Gallery == Eikthyr Trophy Ground.png|Eikthyr Trophy Eikthyr head.png Eikthyr02.jpg Valheim-Eikthyr-Screenshot.jpg File:EikthyrAltar.png == Notes == * Eikthyr is likely a reference to [[wikipedia:Eikþyrnir|Eikþyrnir]], a stag which stands upon Valhalla in Norse mythology. * When Eikthyr's trophy is mounted on an item mount, he will sometimes say, "So you were my death? You look so small and soft... Tell Odin he may have broken this form but the wilderness will never submit to his rules..." * Eikthyr is sometimes known as "deer" in the game files. * In the in-game trophies menu, there is another description of Eikthyr, "Once the king of the forest, the size of the antlers are truly impressive." * Eikthyr is susceptible to [[spirit]] damage, but there are no early game weapons with spirit damage to make use of this weakness. By the time that weapons with spirit damage are available, the player should not have any difficulty fighting Eikthyr anyway. * There is reference to a "Horned One" on one of the [[Runestone]]s that can be found in the [[Meadows]], which can be assumed to be Eikthyr:
''Hold, traveller, and bear witness to my warning. We are many who have come before you, carried here by Odin's will to do his work. The path ahead is hard and the dangers great. If you hold your life dear, keep to these meadows and make your dwelling away from the trees. Fear the Horned One and spare his kin.''

'''Bonemass''' is the third [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a gigantic humanoid mass comprised of toxic ooze, mud and skeletal remains, likely absorbed from nearby tombs situated close to his altar.

== Summoning ==
[[File:BonemassAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Bonemass' Forsaken Altar.]]
Bonemass' [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Swamp]]s. His location can be found when visiting [[Sunken Crypts]] and sometimes ruined structures, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map.

He is summoned by placing 10 {{Item Link|Withered Bone}}s in his Forsaken altar in Swamps. Like all bosses, Bonemass can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Bonemass|Boss strategies#Bonemass}}
Bonemass has an environment aura that forces raining, which means pulling him from the area cannot be used to remove [[Wet Effect|Wet]].

=== Area of effect ===
Bonemass will charge up with a thick green cloud before vomiting a wave of poisonous ooze, inflicting the [[Poison]] status on everything in a 9-meter radius around him (130 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage). This is signaled when he leans backwards. The poison cloud persists for 15 seconds and will continuously refresh the poison duration on any player that stays inside. This effect cannot be dodged or blocked. Bonemass can use this ability when a player is within 15 meters, and it has a cooldown of 30 seconds. The cloud is centered on the impact point of Bonemass's vomit; due to the size of his collision box, this results in the cloud not reaching very far behind him which gives players a safe area to retreat to that is still within range to strike him.

=== Punch ===
A close-range swipe at a player dealing up to 80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 50 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage to players, in addition to 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage to any trees or rocks hit. This attack can be used every 7 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. It hits in a horizontal 8.5-meter 66.1-degree arc in front of Bonemass.

=== Throw ===
At 50-second intervals, Bonemass will reach into his armpit to throw out a glob of goop in the general direction of the player at an initial velocity of 20 meters per second with a spread of 5–20 degrees. On impact, this ability will attempt to spawn four random monsters ([[Skeleton]]s and/or [[Blob]]s, with equal chances for both). A maximum of eight summons of each type can be active at once; but the selection of enemies each spawning instance is still random regardless of the status of spawn caps, meaning reaching the spawn cap for one type of summon will not force spawns for the other. Bonemass will still attempt to summon creatures even if both spawn caps are reached. This ability can only be used when a player is within 30 meters.

== Aftermath ==
Defeating Bonemass provides the player with a Wishbone, which allows the player to easily locate [[Silver Vein]]s beneath the surface of [[Mountain]] biomes (as well as buried [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in Swamp biomes, and other miscellaneous buried treasures in certain locations).

=== Drops ===
{{drop table|{{drop row|item=Bonemass trophy|0star=1}}
{{drop row|item=Wishbone|0star=1 per player online}}|stars=0}}

=== Forsaken power ===
Mounting Bonemass' trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds:

* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Blunt
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Slash
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Pierce
* Block stamina usage: -100%
* Block stamina return: +5

See [[Forsaken_power#Bonemass Power|Bonemass' power]] for more details.

=== Events ===
Defeating Bonemass affects the following [[events]] for that world:

* Disables: Draugr and Skeleton "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: Blobs and Oozers "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: "A skeleton surprise!"
* Enables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." (if [[Moder]] has not been defeated)
* Enables: "There's a smell of sulfur in the air." (if a [[Surtling]] has died)
* Enables: "You are being hunted."
* Enables: "You stirred the cauldron." (if a [[Bat]] has died)
* Enables: "You feel a chill down your spine..."
Note: Two of these events unlock flying enemies that will be uninhibited by base walls and will attack tame animals. For example, bats will quickly wipe out any outdoor tame Boars (if the player has them), most likely before the player can swat them all. Therefore, in order to protect any rare animals (such as a 2-star [[Boar]]), it is advisable to build a secure indoor barn area before undertaking Bonemass.

=== Creature spawning ===
Defeating Bonemass unlocks [[Skeleton]]s to spawn at night in the Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp (additional), Mountain and Plains. They can only have 0 stars.

She appears as a massive frost dragon with black scales, a white fur mane and tattered wings. According to numerous [[Runestone]]s, she is the mother of all [[Drake]]s. == Summoning == [[File:ModerAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Moder's Forsaken Altar.]] Moder's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in the [[Mountain|Mountains]]. Her location can be found when visiting specific ruined structures, typically at the top, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal her nearest summoning location on the map. She is summoned by placing three {{Item Link|Dragon Egg}}s in her Forsaken Altar in the Mountains. Like all bosses, Moder can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met. Considering the extensive weight of dragon eggs (200), purchasing and wearing a [[Megingjord]] from [[Haldor]] will help, as it increases one's carry weight by 150. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Moder|Boss strategies#Moder}} Moder has the ability to fly but will also choose to land, alternating between the two. She is accompanied by an environmental aura that forces [[Freezing Effect]] even in other biomes. === Bite === While grounded, she can bite to deal 120 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 1000 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. This attack has a 30-second cooldown and can only be used when a player is within 7 meters. This hits in an 8-meter 20-degree horizontal arc. === Claw === While grounded, Moder can perform a swipe attack with either claw which deals 110 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 1000 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. This ability is on a 30-second cooldown for each claw, and she must be within 10 meters of a player to use it. The claws hit in a horizontal arc 12 meters in length and 50 degrees in angle. === Ice Barrage === When airborne, every 8 seconds she can fire a barrage of 16 icicles - each projectile travels at 25 meters per second and spreads within 13–20 degrees from the center of her aim dealing 30 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 200 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]], 200 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 200 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. Upon impact with the ground, a crystal forms about as tall as the player and will fall apart 30 seconds later. Each crystal has 10 health and can be destroyed. This attack can be used when a player is within 5–25 meters. === Cold breath === While grounded, she can let forth an icy beam in a 30-meter line which arcs very slightly by 10 degrees. It deals up to 200 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]], 200 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 200 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage and can be used every 8 seconds. She attempts to track the player while using this attack. This ability can be used when a player is within 5–20 meters; this distance is measured from the center of her hitbox, which happens to be roughly 5 meters from her head making it difficult - but still possible - to disable the attack by standing close. == Aftermath == === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Dragon tear|0star=10}} {{drop row|item=Moder trophy|0star=1}}|stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting Moder’s trophy upon her respective stone will allow the player to claim her Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds: * Max carry weight: +300 * Always tailwind while sailing * Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Resistant]] vs Frost * Movement Speed: +10% See [[Forsaken power#Moder Power|Moder's power]] for more details. === Events === Defeating Moder affects the following [[events]] for that world: * Disables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." * Enables: "The horde is attacking!" (if [[Yagluth]] has not been defeated) === Traders === Defeating Moder unlocks the [[Scythe Handle]], [[Toadstool]], [[Fragrant Bundle]] and the [[Mountain Peak Pepper Powder]] from [[The Bog Witch]]. == Gallery == Moder.png ModerTakingFlight.jpg 20210224202752 1.jpg|Moder sitting upon the Altar Moders Stone.jpg|Moder's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] Moder's Altar.jpg 20210224202845 1.jpg 20210224203143 1.jpg 20210224203137 1.jpg == Notes == * Moder is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon dragon] having the typical appearance of a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyvern Wyvern], this is apparent due to both the eggs being dragon eggs, and her tears being dragon tears. * Once summoned, Moder's aura will pause or stop ongoing snowstorms. * In the in-game trophies menu, there is another description of Moder, "Scored with ancient scars, this head was the last sight of countless warriors." * "Moder" translates to "Mother" in Nordic languages. * "Móðr" translates to "anger, grief" in Old Norse. * Moder shares a name with the jötunn daughter of Loki in Adam Nevill's 2011 British novel ''The Ritual'' and its 2017 film adaptation of the same name. * In the game files, "Moder" is known as "dragonqueen". == Achievements == {{Achievement|Boss4Moder}} {{Creatures}} [[de:Drachenmutter]] [[ru:Матерь]] [[cs:Moder]] [[uk:Мати]]

Randomly happening events cause lots of enemies to spawn around the players. Progressing in the game world by defeating bosses causes harder events to appear. Events can be world-based or player-based depending on the world modifier settings in use. World-based events are the default mode.

For most events to end, a player must stay in the active event area until the timer runs out. The event timer is paused if there are no players in the event area (except for the "You are being hunted..." event).

Every 46 minutes there is a 20% chance for a random event;

* Available events are based on which enemies have been [[Global Keys|defeated]] in the game world.
** Most events require defeating a boss to become available (see Enabled by column).
** Some events are permanently disabled after defeating a boss (see Disabled by column).
** Unless player-based raids is enabled, if a raid lists two mobs (e.g. Troll and The Elder), both those mobs must have died on that world for the raid to be enabled.
* If player based raids are enabled:
** Most events are based on which [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]] and materials the player has acquired.
** Some events also check which enemies the player has defeated.
* For each event, check that any of the players fulfills the following conditions:
** The player is in the required biome (see Biome column).
** The player is not in a dungeon.
** The player is within 40 meters of at least 3 [[Player base|base structures]]. This is not required for the "You are being hunted..." event.
* Select a random event from possible events (if any).
* Select a random player from valid players and start the event at the player's position.

== Notes ==

* The event area (96 meters radius) is significantly bigger than the visual red circle (64 meters radius).
** In multiplayer, the event timer ticks when any of the players are in the event area.
** However event enemies are only spawned when the [[Zones|zone]] owner is in the event area.
* Events won't trigger for players who are inside dungeons. Similarly being in a dungeon won't progress events even when inside the event area.
* If an event is already running when a new one triggers, the previous event will automatically end.
* The biome check uses the exact biome at the player's position (which can be seen when hovering the bigger minimap) instead of the average biome based on zone corners (which can be seen on the smaller minimap).
* [[Player base|Base structures]] suppress spawns which affect where enemies can spawn during the events. Large coverage of base structures may completely prevent enemy spawning.
** Enemies are spawned 40-80 meters from players which allows them to spawn outside the event area.
* The source of death for a creature is not tracked. * Tamed creatures can easily be killed during events. For example, the "stirred the cauldron" event which spawns bats is especially dangerous for weaker tamed creatures (such as Boars) held in pens not covered by a roof.

'''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power. 

==[[Eikthyr]] Power==
{{Quote|The grace of the mighty stag flows through you. Your ability to move around is improved, be it on land or in water.}}
60% reduced [[stamina]] usage for running, jumping, and swimming.

==[[The Elder]] Power==
{{Quote|The power of the forest invigorates you. You shall gather its bounties faster, just as you shall regain your own vitality should you lose it.}}
+60% [[Chop]] and [[Pickaxe]] damage increase, +30% health regeneration increase.

==[[Bonemass]] Power==
{{Quote|The mass takes the brunt of your blows. The effort required to raise your shield lessens, and you can withstand harder hits.}}
[[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] (-25%) VS pierce, slash, and blunt damage, -100% [[block]] stamina cost, +5 stamina returned per block.

==[[Moder]] Power==
{{Quote|The dragon's wings urge you on. You shall always have tailwind while sailing, and you shall swiftly carry heavy burdens, even over the coldest mountains.}}
Always tailwind when sailing, +300.0 increased [[carry weight]], +10% increased movement speed, [[Resistance|Resistant]] (-50%) vs frost.

===Notes===
*This power changes the [[wind]] direction while sailing, but not wind intensity. A calm wind will not aid in travel as much as a fast wind.
*The wind direction is only changed while steering the ship. While not in control of a ship, the wind will remain at its regular angle.
*The wind change is local to each player carrying the buff and does not affect each other's wind direction.
*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].

==[[Yagluth]] Power==
{{Quote|The fallen king lends you his might. A king must have the power to vanquish his foes, just as he must be able to support his people.}}
Resistant (-50%) vs lightning, +25 [[Farming (skill)]], and +10% increased damage.

{{Quote|Her Majesty blesses you. In her shadow both stealth and magic may flourish, and no poison shall harm you.}}
+100% [[Eitr]] regeneration increase, -100% [[sneak]] stamina usage, and resistant (-50%) vs poison.

He appears 12 seconds after the offering. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Kall Fimbulbringer|Boss strategies#Kall Fimbulbringer}} The encounter has three phases, each with its own health pool: 10,000 health in phase 1, 7,000 in phase 2 and 30,000 in phase 3, for a total of 47,000. When phase 1 dies, phase 2 takes its place, and phase 3 replaces phase 2 in the same way. Kall Fimbulbringer can't be staggered in any phase. When he first notices a player, the message "His hatred corrupts all!" is shown to all players. When phase 3 is defeated, the message "Peace settles over the world" is shown. ===Phase 1=== Kall Fimbulbringer attacks the player directly. In this phase it is resistant to [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]] and [[Damage types#Lightning|Lightning]] damage and immune to [[Damage types#Spirit|Spirit]] damage. * '''Chain Slam''': 160 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 300 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. There are left and right variants, each as a single and a double slam, all with the same damage. Each variant can be used every three seconds within 12 meters. The single slams are only used at 50% health or more, the double left slam only at 75% health or less, and the double right slam only at 50% health or less. * '''Chain Whirl''': an area attack dealing 150 Blunt, 20 Frost, 300 Chop and 300 Pickaxe damage. It can be used every 10 seconds within 8 meters. * '''Chain Rush''': 125 Blunt, 125 Pierce, 300 Chop and 300 Pickaxe damage. It can be used every 10 seconds within 1–12 meters. * '''Double Sweep''': 150 Blunt, 200 Chop and 200 Pickaxe damage. It can be used every three seconds within 2–12 meters. ===Phase 2=== Kall Fimbulbringer hides inside an invincible block of ice. In this phase it is immune to all damage types that players deal. During this phase, spirits of the previous [[Boss]]es, called aspects, are summoned. They have most of the abilities of the original bosses, although not all of them. The first aspect is the Aspect of the Lightning Stag ([[Eikthyr]]) alone. When it is defeated, the Aspect of the Living Forest ([[The Elder]]) and the Aspect of the Writhing Dead ([[Bonemass]]) appear together. Each of these two is followed by another aspect when defeated: the Living Forest by the Aspect of the Dragon Mother ([[Moder]]) and then the Aspect of the Crawling Matriarch ([[The Queen]]), and the Writhing Dead by the Aspect of the Twisted Soul ([[Yagluth]]) and then the Aspect of the Emerald Flame ([[Fader]]). {| class="wikitable" !
